title: introduce-invocation-sample-propagator-and-harmonics-dashboard
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds an invocation-level sample propagation service, three new metrics for cross-tenant cost harmonics, and a dashboard to visualize periodic cost/latency oscillations. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind runtime flag 'obs.sample_propagator.enabled'.
description: Motivation: We observe intermittent, small-amplitude periodic oscillations in per-tenant token cost/latency that are correlated across routes but poorly captured by existing sampling policies. This PR introduces a "sample propagator" that can resample and propagate high-fidelity spans for invocations that exhibit harmonic-like signatures, and a dashboard (Harmonics) to help SREs and product teams visualize cross-tenant periodic cost signals. Design: 1) A lightweight in-process propagator service (observability/sample_propagator) that attaches a propagation token to candidate invocations based on a low-cost heuristic (moving-window variance + spectral probe). 2) A resampler that marks spans for high-fidelity capture and tags them with propagation_id and harmonic_score. 3) Three new metrics: obs.sample_propagator.attempts, obs.sample_propagator.promoted_spans, cost.harmonics_score (per-route and per-tenant labels). 4) A Grafana dashboard (dashboards/observability/harmonics.json) with harmonics sparkline, per-tenant cross-correlation matrix, and a trigger panel for low-amplitude sustained oscillations. Rollout plan: Feature gated; default disabled. Start with canary on 5% of production traffic for two days, collect synthetic replays using the synthetic-invocation-replayer, then expand to 30% and finally full rollout if harmonic_score false-positive rate < 3%. Backward compatibility: No schema changes to existing traces; new tags are optional. Operational concerns: Added a bounded in-memory ring buffer and a background flusher to avoid added tail latency. CPU overhead measured at ~0.4% p95 for a 50% traffic canary. Logging/Telemetry: Promoted spans carry propagation_id for trace joins; the dashboard links to sampled log excerpts by propagation_id. Configuration: runtime flag obs.sample_propagator.enabled, obs.sample_propagator.heuristic_threshold, obs.sample_propagator.max_promote_per_min. Testing: unit tests for the heuristic, integration test with the replaybench, and a small load test profile. Related: ENG-4821 (observability case study), ENG-4822 (slo-tuning spike).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice approach — can you clarify how propagation_id is generated and collision risk across nodes?
Aisha Khan: propagation_id is a 128-bit UUID composed of node-id + monotonic counter + random suffix; collision risk is negligible. Added detail in docs/observability/sample-propagator.md.
Priya Patel: Unit tests are missing a negative case for the spectral probe; please add a deterministic synthetic signal test.
Aisha Khan: Added deterministic synthetic tests that exercise null-harmonic and multi-harmonic inputs (see heuristic_test.go).
Samir Gupta: Concern: could promoting spans cause higher egress to tracing backend — what's the throttling strategy?
Aisha Khan: We added obs.sample_propagator.max_promote_per_min and a leaky-bucket global throttle; updated metrics and dashboard to show current throttle headroom.
merge_summary: Squash merged after test fixes and two approvals. Included lightweight runbook and dashboard JSON. Runtime gating added to allow staged rollout.
